gaps.sentence: I will note the reference number in case I ___ it later.
gaps.hint: in case means as a precaution
gaps.explanation: 'In case' describes a precaution and takes the present simple: need.

gaps.sentence: If you had set an alarm, you ___.
gaps.explanation: The present result of a past unreal condition takes 'would not be': would not still be asleep.

gaps.sentence: If we ___ tickets today, they will cost half the price.
gaps.explanation: The condition is present simple; only the result clause uses 'will': book.

gaps.sentence: If the pain ___, stop taking the tablets and call your doctor.
gaps.hint: medical instruction with present after if
gaps.explanation: Conditional instructions use the present simple in the if-clause: gets worse.

gaps.sentence: I will write down the address in case I ___ it.
gaps.explanation: 'In case' describes a precaution against a possibility and takes the present simple: forget.

gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.

gaps.sentence: If he had not left his passport at home, he ___ the earlier flight.
gaps.hint: third conditional result, would have participle
gaps.explanation: The unreal past result takes 'would have' plus the participle: would have caught.

gaps.sentence: Should you ___ any problems, please contact support.
gaps.explanation: 'Should you plus infinitive' is a formal way to say 'If you ...': experience.
